pricesSource.title: ERCOT load zone settlement point prices, real-time, hourly

tariff.sourceTitle: Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC, PUCT Monthly Report, as of November 1, 2026
tariff.note: Oncor is the largest wires company in ERCOT and is used here as the example. CenterPoint, AEP Texas and TNMP publish their own rates, and the city utilities and co-ops (Austin Energy, CPS Energy, LCRA, Rayburn) set their own.

rules.title: 16 TAC 25.192, transmission service rates
rules.what: A transmission provider's rate is its approved cost of service divided by the average of ERCOT's coincident peak demand in June, July, August and September (4CP).

rules.title: PUCT Project 58000, proposal for publication, 9 July 2026
rules.what: Would replace the four coincident peak (4CP) method with a twelve coincident peak (12CP) method for assigning transmission costs. Not adopted as a rule when this was built.

peaks.note: The highest hour of ERCOT demand in each of June, July, August and September, from ERCOT's hourly native load file. ERCOT sets the official 4CP on fifteen-minute intervals, so its times can differ from these by part of an hour.

queue.what: ERCOT large-load interconnection status. The deck does not say these loads are data centers. County and customer names are not in the slides that this build could read.

byZone.note: ERCOT did not split this bar into Houston, South, or the NOIE load zones.
